one: A theory course on deep generative models: the probabilistic foundations and training algorithms behind VAEs, GANs, flows, and diffusion.
pos: CS 236 is one of the most systematic courses on generative modeling, taught by Stefano Ermon. It starts from probabilistic modeling and variational inference and covers VAEs, GANs, normalizing flows, energy-based models, and diffusion/score matching; the math load is high.
topics: **Probability foundations**: maximum likelihood, variational inference, ELBO, MCMC
**GANs**: adversarial training, mode collapse, Wasserstein GAN
**Flow models**: invertible transforms, Jacobians, continuous flows
prereq: At least one of CS 221/228/229/230; probability and calculus; Python programming.
assess: Assignments plus a midterm/final and a project; both derivations and implementation matter. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: People working on diffusion models, image/video generation, or generative AI research; anyone who wants the probabilistic ideas behind VAEs and GANs.
tips: Brush up on variational inference and score matching first, or the diffusion part will be rough. Pair with CS 236G for the engineering details of GANs.
